method.shortlist: walk-forward P&L > 0, t >= 1.5, >= 50 trades, >= half of test folds profitable
rules: Only data from before the holdout was used to pick any setting; the holdout (the most recent ~25% of days, one calendar cut for every series in a part) was run once per candidate with frozen settings.

Golden needs ALL of the following. (1) Made money on the holdout with a t-stat of at least 2.5, the strict bar that corrects for every candidate taken to the holdout in lab4 (one-sided Bonferroni, 5%).

(2) There is no live strategy on these markets, so the comparison is the CONTROL: the live bell-curve fair-value model re-tuned on the same search window (lab3 family fv_ref) and run on the same holdout. A new family must beat the control on the same scope on BOTH holdout profit and t-stat. The control itself is judged on the other tests.
(3) Where older Kalshi archive data was downloaded for the series (before Sep 4), it also made money there with t >= 2 on at least 50 trades, with no re-tuning.
(4) No more than 40% of its holdout profit came from a single day.
(5) Economically meaningful after fees: at least $0.10 per $10 trade and at least $2 a day on the holdout.
Pass = made money on the holdout with t >= 2 but missed at least one golden test. Fail = anything else.

Every result assumes $10 per trade (10 contracts per leg for the two-leg pair trades), Kalshi taker fees ceil(0.07*C*P*(1-P)) on every leg (maker 0.0175 for maker rules), fills only at the quoted ask/bid at the end of the decision minute, one bet per market. 'One minute late' re-runs the frozen rule with a 1-minute delay; reported, not graded.
caveats: Short histories. Free 1-minute prices (Yahoo) only go back about 30 days, so every series is tested on roughly Oct 6 - Nov 3 2026 (about 20 trading days) even where Kalshi has older markets: search ~3 weeks, holdout the last 7 days. Treasury yields have only 15 days of Kalshi markets at all (search ~1 week). A t-stat on 7 days is fragile even when it clears the bar; treat anything that passes as 'worth paper trading', never as proven.

The underlying prices are NOT the settlement feed. Kalshi settles these markets on Pyth, whose history API needs a key; Dukascopy's free feed was unreachable from this machine. Yahoo 1-minute bars are used instead: spot quotes for FX, front-month futures for metals/energy, Treasury futures of the matching tenor (inverted) for yields. The model's strike is the feed's own price at the market open. coins[*].feed_sign_agreement_search shows how often the feed's 15-minute move has the same sign as Kalshi's result (e.g. ~96% for EUR/USD): every disagreement is a likely loss for a fair-value rule, so these backtests understate what a bot with a Pyth feed could do, and a failure here does not prove there is no edge with the right feed.
Yahoo's AUD/USD and some futures (palladium, platinum) skip minutes; gaps are forward-filled, so the 'price now' can be up to a minute or two stale on those series.

Backtest fills assume the quoted ask had enough size for a $10 order (10 contracts a leg for set trades). The yields are thin (median ~200 contracts per market, 11-15% of markets never trade), so real fills would be worse. The one-minute-late column shows how much survives if the bot acts a minute later.

Structural arbitrage: every non-crypto 15-minute series has exactly one market per 15-minute window (one 'at or above the open' contract), so there is no ladder or range to arbitrage. The range-sum test was run on the only 15-minute series with mutually exclusive outcomes, Kalshi's crypto 'coin race' (KXCRYPTOLEAD15M). The 15-min vs hourly pair and hourly-ladder tests (xmkt_arb, xmkt_fv, ladder_arb) were run earlier on crypto data and are kept for completeness.

Stock-index 15-minute series (S&P 500, Nasdaq-100, Dow) and USD/MXN are listed by Kalshi but had no settled markets, so they could not be tested. Brent has only 13 days of markets (< 14) and was not tested.
To fit the time budget the lab3 parameter grids were thinned to every 3rd configuration (method.grid_thinning); neighbouring configurations in those grids are near-duplicates.

families.name: Live model, re-tuned (control)
families.idea: The model already live (bell-curve fair value vs the ask), re-tuned on a wider grid. It is the control: a new idea has to do better than simply re-tuning what we have.
families.finding: Nothing reached the holdout: no scope had a good enough walk-forward record.

families.name: Fat-tail fair value
families.idea: Price the contract with a fat-tailed (Student-t) distribution instead of the bell curve, so big moves before the close count as more likely. Long shots have been winning live.
families.finding: Nothing reached the holdout: no scope had a good enough walk-forward record.

families.name: Bootstrap fair value
families.idea: No formula: the chance of finishing above the strike is read off this coin's own recent history of similar-sized moves (last 7 or 21 days of 1-minute prices).
families.finding: Nothing reached the holdout: no scope had a good enough walk-forward record.

families.name: Recalibrated fair value
families.idea: Stretch or squash the model's probabilities toward or away from 50% (a calibration slope) to correct a model that is systematically over- or under-confident.
families.finding: Nothing reached the holdout: no scope had a good enough walk-forward record.

families.name: Better volatility
families.idea: Same model, but measure volatility better: exponentially weighted, high/low range (Parkinson), jump-robust (bipower), shorter windows, or the larger of 1h and 4h.
families.finding: Nothing reached the holdout: no scope had a good enough walk-forward record.

families.name: Time-of-day volatility
families.idea: Crypto is calmer at some hours than others. Scale volatility by how this 15-minute slot of the day has behaved over the previous two weeks.
families.finding: Nothing reached the holdout: no scope had a good enough walk-forward record.

families.name: Settlement-average timing
families.idea: Kalshi settles on an average of the final minute, which leaves less real time for the price to move than the clock says. Shorten (or lengthen) the time left in the model.
families.finding: Nothing reached the holdout: no scope had a good enough walk-forward record.

families.name: Momentum-aware fair value
families.idea: Assume part of the coin's last few minutes of movement carries on (or reverses) and build that drift into the fair value.
families.finding: Best: Copper · Momentum-aware fair value (18c edge, 100% of last 10-min move carries on, vol x0.8): $167 at t = 0.82 on the holdout (fail).

families.name: Dynamic edge
families.idea: Ask for a bigger (or smaller) mispricing depending on minutes left, the bid-ask spread and the price level, instead of one fixed 12-cent gap.
families.finding: Nothing reached the holdout: no scope had a good enough walk-forward record.

families.name: Volatility-regime filter
families.idea: Only trade when short-term volatility is clearly above (rising) or below (calming) the 4-hour level.
families.finding: Nothing reached the holdout: no scope had a good enough walk-forward record.

families.name: Spread / stale-quote filter
families.idea: Only trade when the Kalshi spread is tight, and/or only when the quote has (or has not) just moved, and/or contracts actually traded that minute.
families.finding: Nothing reached the holdout: no scope had a good enough walk-forward record.

families.name: Fresh spot move, lagging quote
families.idea: Only trade when the gap was opened by a spot move in the last 1-2 minutes (the model jumped) and, optionally, the Kalshi quote has not yet followed.
families.finding: Best: Copper · Fresh spot move, lagging quote (11c edge, spot moved in last 1 min, quote lagging): $181 at t = 0.68 on the holdout (fail).

families.name: Jump trigger
families.idea: Only trade right after a sudden 1-minute jump in spot (when Kalshi is most likely to lag), or only in calm minutes.
families.finding: Nothing reached the holdout: no scope had a good enough walk-forward record.

families.name: Session / weekday filter
families.idea: Live model limited to certain hours of the day (Asia, Europe, US, late US) or to weekdays or weekends only.
families.finding: Nothing reached the holdout: no scope had a good enough walk-forward record.

families.name: Previous-window filter
families.idea: Only take the fair-value trade when the previous 15-minute window moved the same way as the bet (trend) or the opposite way (reversal), by at least a set number of standard deviations.
families.finding: Best: Copper · Previous-window filter (5c edge, previous 15 min moved the same way, vol x0.8, 10-90c only): $139 at t = 0.69 on the holdout (fail).

families.name: Ensemble of live-style models
families.idea: Run several fair-value models side by side (bell curve, blended volatility, edge vs the bid, fat-tail) and take the first signal, or only signals two models agree on. One bet per market.
families.finding: Nothing reached the holdout: no scope had a good enough walk-forward record.

families.name: Exit before settlement
families.idea: Buy on the same mispricing, then sell back at the bid once the price has converged to fair value, hit a profit target, or at a set minute, instead of holding to the close. Pays the taker fee both ways.
families.finding: Best: Copper · Exit before settlement (12c edge, sell once the bid reaches fair value, vol x0.8, 10-90c only): $166 at t = 0.74 on the holdout (fail).

families.name: Limit order at fair value minus edge
families.idea: Instead of paying the ask, rest a bid at (fair value - edge) for a few minutes; filled only if a seller comes down to it. Cheaper fee, but misses trades and risks bad fills.
families.finding: Nothing reached the holdout: no scope had a good enough walk-forward record.

families.name: Live model as a maker
families.idea: The live model's signal, but executed by resting a bid at the best bid (+1c) for 1-3 minutes instead of buying at the ask.
families.finding: Best: Copper · Live model as a maker (18c edge, bid rests 1 min, vol x0.8): $575 at t = 1.74 on the holdout (fail).

families.name: Edge-scaled stakes
families.idea: Live model, but bet more when the model's edge is bigger (fractional Kelly), capped at 2-5x the average stake. Stakes are scaled so the average is about $10, to stay comparable.
families.finding: Nothing reached the holdout: no scope had a good enough walk-forward record.

families.name: Per-coin tuning with shrinkage
families.idea: One rule for all 9 coins, but each coin gets its own settings, chosen by that coin's own results plus the all-coin average (shrinkage), so thin data can't drive it alone.
families.finding: Nothing reached the holdout: no scope had a good enough walk-forward record.

families.name: Ensemble of the best survivors
families.idea: For each coin, combine the 2-3 families with the best walk-forward record into one first-to-fire rule (one bet per market).
families.finding: Best: Copper · Ensemble of the best survivors: $165 at t = 0.71 on the holdout (fail).

families.name: Crypto: 15-min vs hourly pair (arbitrage)
families.idea: The 15-minute market that closes on the hour and the hourly 'above K' ladder settle on the same price. Buying 15-min YES plus hourly NO at a strike at or above the 15-min strike (or the mirror pair) pays at least $1 whatever happens; trade it when the two quotes leave a margin.
families.finding: Nothing reached the holdout: no scope had a good enough walk-forward record.

families.name: Crypto: 15-min priced off the hourly ladder
families.idea: Read the market's own probability for the 15-minute strike off the hourly ladder (interpolating between the nearest hourly strikes) and buy the 15-minute side that is cheaper than that.
families.finding: Nothing reached the holdout: no scope had a good enough walk-forward record.

families.name: Crypto: Hourly ladder monotonicity
families.idea: Inside one hourly ladder a higher strike can never be more likely than a lower one. When a higher strike's YES bid sits above a lower strike's YES ask, buy YES low + NO high (pays at least $1).
families.finding: Nothing reached the holdout: no scope had a good enough walk-forward record.

families.name: Coin-race outcomes summing to $1 (arbitrage)
families.idea: In Kalshi's 15-minute 'which coin rises most' race exactly one of the five outcomes pays. If the five YES asks add up to less than $1 (or the five NO asks to less than $4), buying the whole set locks in the difference; trade when that margin after fees is at least g.
families.finding: Nothing reached the holdout: no scope had a good enough walk-forward record.
